title: What MCC covers
text: 50% AIQ contributed by participating state government colleges; 100% deemed and participating DNB seats; central-university/institute seats with their own internal eligibility. INI-CET is separate. “All MCC seats” is not the same as “50% state-government AIQ”.

title: Central reservation, not Telangana’s roster
text: AIQ: SC 15%, ST 7.5%, Central-list OBC-NCL 27%, EWS 10%; PwD 5% horizontal. State BC status alone is not Central OBC-NCL proof. No general women’s quota is listed in this AIQ reservation table. Deemed/minority/NRI and internal seats require their own rules.

title: Float is online joining in 2026
text: Submit Float willingness, upload clear mandatory documents and contact the allotted institute’s nodal officer. The institute verifies online. Resolve queries within the reporting window and retain the provisional seat-confirmation record. The bulletin calls for uploads within 2–3 days of final allotment so discrepancies can be resolved; the overall reporting deadline still controls.

title: Freeze requires physical reporting
text: Physically report with original documents and admission fees at the allotted institute. A final allotment letter or a Float click alone does not replace completion of joining.

title: Keep the Round 1 seat while seeking an upgrade
text: A properly joined Round 1 Float candidate may fill fresh Round 2 choices. If no upgrade occurs, the existing seat is retained. If you decide against Round 2 upgrading, FAQ 19 says not to fill fresh choices; verify the portal status. This retains a seat, not an indefinite right to free resignation.

title: Upgrades are binding replacements
text: On a Round 2 upgrade, the old Round 1 seat is automatically cancelled; it cannot be reclaimed. Obtain the online relieving record and complete joining of the new seat. Even a category upgrade at the same college needs fresh admission formalities. Non-joining of the upgraded seat forfeits security.

title: Switching to a state seat
text: The Round 1/2 scheme permits participation in state counselling. To take a state allotment, surrender the MCC seat formally: Float resignation online; Freeze resignation physically at the institute. Use the MCC-notified resignation period and save the accepted/generated record. A state allotment does not automatically resign MCC.

title: Round 1 free exit has a time limit for joined candidates
text: A Round 1 non-joiner can free exit. A joined candidate must use the formal resignation process within the period prescribed by MCC. The checked documents do not publish a separate exact resignation cut-off for every cross-counselling switch. Do not substitute the reporting deadline for an unannounced resignation deadline.

title: Round 2: forfeiture; further entry needs fresh payment
text: Non-joining or surrender of a Round 2 allotment forfeits security. The scheme permits eligible candidates who resigned/exited Round 2 to participate in Round 3 with fresh payment. Resignation still requires a permitted window.

title: Round 3 and Stray are commitment rounds
text: Non-joining a Round 3 seat forfeits security and eliminates further MCC participation. Joined Round 3 seats cannot be resigned. Stray allotment must be joined or security is forfeited. Eligibility for Stray also depends on prior allotments/joined status and Centre–State data sharing.

title: Retained Float seats must physically join after Round 3
text: After Round 3, physical reporting is mandatory for fresh/upgraded Round 3 allottees and Round 1/2 Float candidates who did not upgrade. Online Float cannot be continued indefinitely.

title: AIQ plus deemed: only the higher MCC payment is prescribed
text: FAQ 9 says candidates opting for both pay only ₹5,000 registration plus ₹2 lakh security. It does not prescribe ₹25,000 plus ₹2 lakh as two independently protected deposits. If both were collected, reconcile receipts with MCC/HLL; do not assume a government allotment limits forfeiture to ₹25,000.

title: Refunds follow completion of counselling
text: Eligible security refunds return to the original payment account after counselling, not immediately after each round. Keep that account/card active. Registration fees are non-refundable; tuition refunds and college bond liabilities are separate. The refund FAQ describes initiation within 15 days/working days and completion within 30 days of the relevant MCC notification/list.

title: 2026 change explicitly identified by MCC
text: Chapter 3 contrasts the 2025 physical process with the new 2026 Freeze/Float workflow. Use its online-joining and online Float-resignation instructions alongside the round rules; generic physical-reporting text elsewhere in the bulletin must be read in that context.

title: MCC admission does not erase a college/state bond
text: MCC directs candidates to confirm course fees, stipend, service obligations and bond amounts with the institution before choices. The state-government AIQ service policy, central institution, deemed college and DNB hospital can differ. Use the State bonds page for dated evidence, then confirm the actual 2026 contract.

title: Local eligibility must be documented
text: Local means at least four consecutive years of Telangana study ending in the relevant qualifying examination, subject to the stated exceptions. A Telangana UG-local entrant studying at the specified outside state-wide institution can qualify; a non-local-quota MBBS entrant in Telangana is not automatically local. Other-state candidates are ineligible. Your Telangana MBBS/local claim needs the prescribed study and admission records.

title: Seat pools: government versus private
text: The state-government share follows exclusion of contributed AIQ seats (normally 50% AIQ / 50% state under the MCC scheme). Private colleges have a 50% Competent Authority share alongside a separate 50% management share. Do not apply a private 50% split to government seats or double count women/service reservations as extra seats. Exact branch counts await the current KNRUHS matrix.

title: Vertical and horizontal reservations
text: SC 15% split as SC1 1%, SC2 9%, SC3 5%; ST 10%; BC 29% split A 7%, B 10%, C 1%, D 7%, E 4%. Women 33⅓% and PwD 5% are horizontal. Minority-college seats are for eligible Muslim-minority candidates. The displayed EWS qualifying score is not evidence of a separate 10% EWS seat allocation in this prospectus.

title: In-service seats are a separate horizontal claim
text: 20% in clinical broad specialties and 30% in pre/para-clinical broad specialties are reserved horizontally for eligible in-service candidates under the cited service rules. These are not extra seats, and an ordinary fresh applicant cannot claim them.

title: Qualification, internship and existing PG study
text: NEET-PG 2026 qualification, completed internship by 30 September 2026 and permanent Telangana State Medical Council registration are required. The prospectus excludes candidates already studying PG degree/diploma/DNB; get KNRUHS clarification before assuming an existing PG enrolment or cross-counselling switch is eligible. A same-cycle MCC option does not override state conditions.

title: Separate application and web options
text: Complete CQ registration, payment and certificate uploads; print the application. Provisional/final merit and web-option schedules are published separately. A qualified list or registration is not an allotment. At admission submit originals, application printout and self-attested copies at the allotted college.

title: University fee and tuition are separate
text: Pay ₹35,000 university fee to download the allotment letter. Tuition is as notified by Telangana and varies by institution/course category. The registration/processing fee is non-refundable. The reviewed prospectus does not establish a separate universally refundable security deposit or the refund treatment of every university-fee situation.

title: Do not import MCC’s free-exit rules
text: The CQ prospectus refers to the last date for Free Exit but does not provide that date in the reviewed registration documents. Await the phase-specific KNRUHS notice for reporting, sliding, resignation and exit deadlines. Leaving after the stated free-exit limit attracts the prospectus discontinuation terms.

title: Course discontinuation: ₹50 lakh, with additional conditions
text: The admission bond states ₹50 lakh on default in completing training and refund of stipend/salary received. Discontinuation after free exit also carries a three-year KNRUHS PG counselling debarment. These are not small registration-deposit penalties; read the signed bond and applicable exit notice.

title: One-year service after completion
text: Non-service postgraduates must serve the Government of Telangana for one year if required under the government orders. The admission service bond is ₹20 lakh for a PG degree and ₹10 lakh for a diploma. This is separate from the ₹50 lakh course-completion bond.

title: AP domicile is not an automatic state-quota entitlement
text: The 2026 prospectus uses G.O.148 dated 28 October 2024 and the local-candidate rules. Do not carry forward an old shared AP/Telangana non-local entitlement. The state-wide-institution exception and non-local UG exclusion must be read exactly. SC subgrouping cites an April 2025 order: neither provision should be advertised as newly introduced in 2026 without the amendment history.

title: Private management share and the correct denominators
text: Management is 50% of each private college’s specialty seats: MQ1 is 25%, MQ2/NRI 15%, MQ3/institutional 10% of the TOTAL seats. Within MQ1 only, 85% is Telangana-local reserved and 15% nationally open. As an illustration on 100 total seats, these are 21.25 local MQ1 + 3.75 open MQ1 + 15 MQ2 + 10 MQ3, with actual seats rounded by the official roster/matrix.

title: Local reservation is different from caste reservation
text: MQ has no SC/ST/BC community reservation and no other general reservations listed; reserved-category cut-offs affect exam qualification only. The explicit MQ1 local/open split still applies. Minority-college seats go to eligible Muslim-minority candidates; non-minority conversion is described only for the last phase if eligible minority candidates are unavailable.

title: MQ1, MQ2 and MQ3 are not interchangeable
text: MQ1 includes national applicants subject to the 85/15 local split. MQ2 requires the specified NRI/OCI/NRI-sponsorship proof. MQ3 requires a principal’s sponsorship and the defined institutional connection: own MBBS graduate, employee or employee’s son/daughter. Paying a higher fee alone does not establish MQ2/MQ3 eligibility.

title: Medical registration and internship
text: Recognised MBBS, NEET-PG 2026 qualification, internship completed by 30 September 2026 and permanent Telangana State Medical Council registration are required. Upload documents at application; do not rely on a later opportunity to cure missing eligibility.

title: ₹15,000 application; university fee on allotment
text: Registration/processing is ₹15,000 plus transaction charges, non-refundable. Clinical university fees: MQ1 ₹2 lakh; MQ2/MQ3 ₹3 lakh. Non-clinical: MQ1 ₹75,000; MQ2/MQ3 ₹1 lakh. These university fees are paid to download the allotment order, separate from annual tuition, and are not described as MCC-style refundable security deposits.

title: ₹23 lakh is not a verified universal 2026 tuition
text: The 2026 prospectus says tuition is government-notified. The checked G.O.107 explicitly covers the 2023–2026 block and shows college/category variation, including ₹23 lakh and ₹24 lakh clinical Cat-B examples. Do not silently apply that expired block to 2026–27 or apply clinical rates to Pathology/Biochemistry. Confirm the current order and college invoice before choices.

title: MQ needs its own registration
text: CQ registration does not register you for MQ. Apply and upload at pvttspgmed.tsche.in by 30 October, 4 PM IST. The notification includes KNRUHS private colleges and Neelima Institute affiliated to Anurag University. Current MQ merit, options, allotment and reporting dates are to be notified separately.

title: ₹50 lakh discontinuation liability
text: The admission completion bond is ₹50 lakh. The prospectus explicitly imposes ₹50 lakh plus a three-year KNRUHS counselling bar for discontinuation after the second phase of counselling or later. Do not infer a first-phase no-cost resignation deadline: obtain the phase notice and institution refund terms before a switch.

title: One-year senior residency at the same institution
text: The prospectus requires the admitted candidate to undertake one year as Senior Resident at the institution where the PG course was pursued after successful completion. This differs from CQ government-service wording. Confirm the actual agreement, appointment/pay and any institutional applicability before admission.

title: Local MQ1 split is now explicit in the current prospectus
text: The 2026 document cites G.O.200 and G.O.201 dated 3 November 2025 for the 85%-local/15%-open split within MQ1, using G.O.148 for local status. This is a current rule with a 2025 order date, not proof that local preference began only in 2026. Exact 2026 counts await the phase matrix.

title: Your main route is open private seats
text: 50% of total private-college seats are open to eligible NEET-PG candidates with an NMC-recognised MBBS from anywhere. The other private half and the state-government share have Rajasthan MBBS / specified government-service eligibility through Round 3. Telangana domicile alone does not qualify for those restricted seats.

title: Government AIQ and Rajasthan private AI are different
text: 50% of government/government-society/RUHS CMS seats go through MCC AIQ; remaining state seats and all private seats go through the Rajasthan Board. A private seat labelled “AI nature” is Rajasthan counselling, not an MCC allotment. Management labels in government-society institutions do not waive state eligibility.

title: Out-of-state applicants are UR for state-category benefits
text: Rajasthan’s SC/ST/OBC-NCL/MBC-NCL/EWS benefits are for eligible bonafide Rajasthan candidates. Other-state category candidates are considered UR and must qualify as UR. The booklet states at least 25% women within each category and 5% horizontal PwD; do not assume a Telangana caste certificate or every state reservation benefit transfers to the open-private route.

title: Internship and council registration
text: Internship must finish by 30 September 2026. Valid NMC/MCI/state council registration is required; if registered with another state initially, submit Rajasthan Medical Council registration within one month after joining. State-process Post-MBBS DNB/diploma seats are only for regular Rajasthan government in-service candidates, separate from MCC DNB.

title: Private choices need one ₹5 lakh security payment
text: Application is ₹4,000 plus charges for your out-of-state route. Private-college choices require ₹5 lakh security in one transaction. The ₹1 lakh government and ₹2 lakh government-society/RUHS management tiers do not need to be added to ₹5 lakh; depositing the higher tier permits lower-tier choices only where otherwise eligible.

title: Security is adjustable against tuition after joining
text: On joining, Rajasthan security is adjusted against tuition. If neither forfeited nor adjusted, it is refunded to the original payment account after counselling. Reconcile the allotment-letter demand and Board payment instructions so adjustment is not confused with a second tuition charge. Registration is non-refundable.

title: Report at SMS Jaipur, with one-year tuition
text: Report in person at the allotted-college desk, Academic Block, SMS Medical College, Jaipur, within the schedule. Pay the complete first-year tuition via NEFT/RTGS to the Board account printed on the allotment letter; bring proof, originals, copies and bonds. Downloading the allotment is not joining. The booklet requires accepted resignation/relieving from another current institution.

title: Round 1 free exit; retained seats acquire later-round obligations
text: Non-joining Round 1 does not forfeit security. A joined Round 1 candidate who is not upgraded in Round 2 (or does not participate) may resign without forfeiture within two days of the Round 2 result. After that, the retained seat is treated under Round 2 rules. Formal portal-generated resignation is necessary; offline resignation is not accepted.

title: Round 2 resignation is restricted, not an automatic paid exit
text: Non-joining a fresh/upgraded Round 2 seat forfeits security and further participation requires re-registration and fresh security. Joined Round 2/retained seats generally cannot be resigned except in specifically notified windows (including identified AIQ switches). Do not assume losing ₹5 lakh alone buys permission to leave a joined course.

title: Round 3 and Stray restrictions
text: Round 3 non-joining forfeits security and excludes Stray. Joined/retained Round 3 seats cannot be resigned. Stray non-joining forfeits security and bars further state rounds, with the participation bond terms also relevant. The local-eligibility restriction is relaxed for vacancies after Round 3, but prior allotment/joined-status exclusions remain.

title: Fresh choices and irreversible upgrades
text: Fresh choices are mandatory for Round 2 and Round 3 upgrading. An upgraded seat automatically vacates the earlier seat; originals transfer to the upgraded institution rather than being handed to the candidate. Being content with the old seat after the upgrade does not restore it.

title: Private course-exit surety is separate from security
text: A private-college surety can require remaining-course fees if the course is left mid-way. The booklet prohibits advance fees, post-dated cheques or bank guarantees for the remaining two years. Government non-service seats have separate service/surety bonds. A refundable deposit is not the maximum possible liability.

title: Registration extension overrides only the original registration dates
text: The live notice published 22 October extended Part 1 to 24 October, 4 PM IST and Part 2 to 24 October, 8 PM IST; a 24 October reminder reiterated completion. No new security/choice dates were found in the checked feed. Keep the original Round 1 schedule for those other events, subject to future amendments.
